item.title: Crime Scene Investigation Procedure
item.content:encoded:
Hey howdy hey, so I'm writing a tale at the moment that predominantly revolves around a crime scene. Thing is, I don't actually know very much about how actual crime scene procedures work, as the most popular point of reference tends to be dramatized TV shows.

I realise that in order to keep stuff interesting I'll need to strike a decent balance between real-world procedure and something a little more fictitious, but I'm not entirely sure where to look for real-world references. I've done some research, but I end up with a mixed bag of results that refer to how various countries handle it.

I'm looking for details of crime scene procedure as it would be in the real world particularly for the US - what kinda staff will be present, who's allowed where, how much can be done on-site that would contribute to the investigation, etc.
The crime takes place indoors (an apartment), and involves a dead body, if those details matter at all.

Articles for reference would be good, and if there's any online short story type deals that exist out there (I've had no luck finding any that aren't books) that would be fantastic.

I'd visit the crit forums and try to refine your idea. Reading more recently created SCPs from series 5 and 6 could help give you an idea of the site's writing standards nowadays, too.

item.title: Scp of Future Past, and Everything Else...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:
Scp XXXX is a Reality Bender
Scp XXXX had been discovered in a cave near Quebec, Canada
Scp XXXX is spanned through time and space.

Central Narrative:
Scp XXXX was discovered by an Amateur Cave Explorer in 1973, in a cave near Quebec, Canada. The Amateur Cave Explorer was taken into Foundation custody and amnestisized, alongside all other civilians involved, after reporting to a local hospital, stating he heard a voice in his head talk about freeing himself from the wizards bonds. The Foundation learns Scp XXXX voice spreads into Humans Consciousness when any contact is made beit physical or verbal. The cave of origin is blocked and all Personnel that had been infected had been anesthetized. Scp XXXX is reclassified from euclid to safe. 14 years later, Dr. Mason Cooper reports hearing voices inside his head, though he had only been working for the Foundation for 11 years. Staff had concluded that Personnel already infected by Scp XXXX previously had seemed to get reinfected. Though some personnel had either left the Foundation and been Anesthetized or were somewhere else in the world. Scp XXXX is reclassified as keter as it now spreads into the entire world. As more and more instances of Scp XXXX begin to be heard in peoples head the more mist and fog begins to surround Scp XXXX’s point of origin. Until at a Estimated 1 000 000 cases where the fog slowly turned into a human like form and moved into Montreal, Canada. The Foundation theorizes that Scp XXXX was sent across space and time by the Wizards in 1200, so any Instance of Scp XXXX would imbalance its containment as it would be more in one time then the others, meaning it would start to remeterialize. The Foundation enlists Mobile Task Force Simga 32 ( Tbh I Dont Any Good Mtf Who Travel Through Time ) To travel to Canada and release a amnestic and start a PowerGrid Failure to all of Quebec to stop the spread of Media related to Scp XXXX, Finally Sigma 32 puts down a temporal rift near the anomaly, sending all living creatures in the radius to various points in the future in order to contain it. Scp XXXX is currently pending classification of either safe or neutralized.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The archived containment class would go from euclid to safe to keter to pending, meaning there is lots of story.

Additional Notes: If you could help find a name for the Scp Article and a Mtf that specializes in Time Travel I would be even more grateful, but if you just want to critique I'm still very thankful.

item.title: Re: The Bone Seer
item.content:encoded:
Hey there! Thank you so much for taking the time to go through the concept. I'm glad you like the core. Allow me to address some of the points you made.

+ My feedback
- Collapse

I really like this idea of reading the bones but I am unconvinced about the entire thing centred around a vague K-class event. That's no way to build stakes.

I'm trying to go for the idea that the SCP believes it, with the Foundation very much pointing out their scepticism at the validity of the information. This is not at all what the skip would be centred around. It'd serve to introduce the idea that the use of its abilities has shifted its worldview considerably (I mean, even in real life, we have people believing in various apocalypses), with further interviews reinforcing it. However, if you still think that wouldn't work, I get it. Some ideas from the top of my head could be the SCP worried about something/someone "corrupting the Song of the world" and wanting help from the Foundation, but that might be too vague. My (way back) original idea was the SCP being fascinated by the paranormal and wanting to assist and work in the Foundation, but I feared that would be too X-many - something I was terrified of getting close to.

also not convinced that being sure the world would end would then lead to these results… like maybe the cooperation, but why would it make the SCP apathetic about the individual lives? That's fine if you wanna make them cold towards individual lives, but it doesn't make much sense this would be the reason personally.

I was thinking it would be along the lines of "if everyone is going to be dead soon, no reason to get attached or care", or how in an apocalyptic scenario, which the SCP believes in, you'd not get too close to people as they could die at any moment. Still, it could easily be changed to a personality trait gained from being in contact with so many memories, including those of deaths.

I don't think experiment logs are the way to go here. Instead, you could summarize what research was done with the results and then unpack them in conversations or observation reports from the researchers.

I probably worded that part badly since that's what I was trying to go for. The first set of logs would be with the SCP - Foundation giving it various bones and seeing how much info it can gain from them, experimenting with the species of the bones, how old they are, how mundane they are, as well as how accurately the SCP can glean information by cross-referencing the info. The second set of logs would be D-class being given the "charms" and observing how they handle it - a normal person being exposed to memories of, say, a horse, or a murder victim. Also what psychological traits influence how the "charms" affect people (ie. how does someone with would aphantasia deal with having different memories)

I think some unpacking of the actual anomaly would be more interesting than the focus on some vague end of the world.

Again, I think I just phrased it really badly since the other gentleperson above also got that impression. The K-class is by no means the focus of the skip - it's there to explain why the SCP turned in to the Foundation and what motivates it, but beyond the Foundation expressing strong scepticism towards these claims and introducing the idea of the SCP being affected by its abilities, that's it. The meat of the story would very much be talking to the SCP and seeing how its abilities work on it and others.

Please, let me know if any of these replies convinced you/better explained about some part of the skip, or if you're still not sold about some of them working, so I can start thinking of ways to change and modify the concepts. Again, thank you very much for taking the time!

item.title: Re: (Awaiting greenlights) The elite soldier.
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

The first suit was tested, the U.S. army closed the deal off after they saw what horrible things the suit can do.

What horrible things? There's kinda an implication that this can do many different things but I don't really have a feel for what.

Only 3 were made two are still lost and the third one a soldier still wears.

What does 'lost' mean here? Like, 'missing'? Or 'destroyed'? If it's the first, why is no-one else looking for it?

This feels…a little unsatisfying to me. On one level, there's some thematic weirdness: there's this like, sense that the SCP is a dude who just, wants to do his best and is a big dang hero that everyone loves, except the US army found it too horrifying to use and so there's this disconnect between the angle of 'the foundation will do anything and resort to any means' which feels kinda horrifying and the angle of this dude just being super nice and cool and chill, which feels kinda heartwarming.

On another level: you don't really do anything interesting with this; there's a long investigation section at the start that feels kinda uninteresting because none of the discoveries are particularly novel (since, the discovery would be after the description here: we already know the foundation found a suit and there's a person in it cos guess what, we already read the description) and then there's a vague thing about him joining an MTF. This isn't a bad thing to happen but it's under-utilised: there's no like, extensive training sequence and determined work by the SCP towards convincing the Foundation he can be helpful and uncertainty of whether he'd achieve that; but there's also no real like…cool things happening as a result of them being in a MTF; there's no 'mission log' or anything and I'm left feeling like this just…doesn't have the narrative meat to it for it to work.

Circling back to the themes: I'm really not a fan of the kinda, glorification of the military throughout this. This is, obviously, a personal thing but it's very possible that I just wouldn't like something this 'boo yah go soldiers' even if you had executed it well.

item.title: Buzzcut
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Fantasy

Elevator Pitch: It's a barber buzzer. Upon using it on one's head, the individual starts receiving more attention than usual. Overtime, as hair grows, the attention diminishes, unless one cuts again, and instead attention increases. Attention, as well as sex appeal. Continuing the process allows the user to have increasing and overwhelming charisma to the extent that they can influence first people, then towns, then world events.

Central Narrative: The buzzer was found to be in the possession of an artifact dealer, and was purchased by the owner of a 50's themed diner to be placed in a safe with other memorabilia. Upon discovery by the Foundation, the dive owner says the girl he bought it from claims it was used by Elvis to cut his hair. After testing the piece is found to be non anamolous, placed in confinement, however an agent over the testing steals it to resell it, but not before trying it on his own head. He begins to notice his life change.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fact the the influence builds on itself to make the user more and more powerful, and can be transferred if one single hair is buzzed on another man or woman. The buzzer also increases the physical strength of the individual and performance of physiological functions, to the extent that the user can not only become stronger than possible for a human, but also have a faster metabolism (speed), more god like features, and be a far greater sexy badboy/girl than humanly possible.

Additional Notes: After non-use of about a week, all influence dies out. It isn't saved within the buzzer. This is why, if the Elvis fact is true, Elvis, nor any of the other users' influence, is transferred to new users. Any stretch beyond humanly possible abilities granted by the buzzer is unnoticed by individuals, due to the overwhelming charisma, and is brushed off. There is no proper way to cut your hair with the buzzer, but upon doing so, everyone will love your haircut.

item.title: Re: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
I suppose something I could do is to eliminate all narrative/reasoning portions from this concept and only put down what he is and what he is capable of doing.

+ show block
– hide block

Ok, so here's the problem I'm having right now with this particular project. I'm trying to stay within the template and within the word count. I'm trying not to reveal too much information because if I do, it might seem like a big mess or too much information for someone to swallow in one sitting. The James Devillian Twist SCP project is a big project. I mean… a very big project. He has a wide array of other anomalous abilities and somewhat complicated motivations. He doesn't see someone's destiny. He sees their "supposed" destiny, or what it is that they were meant to do in life, the thing that they are driven towards or driven to do. He sees this along with a ton of other information about that object, including any weaknesses they hold. Twist is a psychopath who will always know how to put his target down.

I read through 049. One major difference here is that through experimentation and interrogation, Twist's "LLUN" threat is verifiable and the second difference is its not a disease. Twist just thinks that if he introduces a small bit of the LLUN's nature to the world, that it might be able to prepare for the upcoming apocalyptic battle with the LLUN, similar to how a vaccine works in a way.

Should I do away with the template and try my own thing with presenting this concept? Use my own format? There isn't really a section in the template for SCP Abilities.

item.title: Re: [Seeking Greenlights] What Follows
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

My concern is that there feels like a big disconnect between 'thing what attacks you if you don't run up the stairs in the dark' and everything about there being some kind of breakthrough that could unlock greater human potential, and between that and the tie in to SCP-5000 and Project PNEUMA. It ends up feeling like this has a lot of interesting little ideas in it but not enough connective tissue to hold it all together or to like, explain the jump from one angle to the next.

I'm also not sure if there's enough narrative meat to like, keep us enticed during this process? Like, even if you do manage to have all the information flow together well, it feels…like this really lacking a big narrative hook to really keep us unboard and prevent this feeling like a big info dump about a weird thing. Part of me wonders whether it might work best as a tale focussed around e.g. a foundation researcher who discovers the start of this and then gradually pieces a lot of disparate information together until they discover the truth of this?

I kinda feel like ending on the mystery of what the Foundation learnt might feel really unsatisfying: it kinda feels like the whole thing is built around this mystery and making the reader think about it, and not having a solid answer here feels…like it might end up feeling kinda analogous to reading every chapter of an Agatha Christie book except the final one where you find out who done it.

I think at the end of the day, the lack of purpose is my biggest issue with this concept: there's some really cool flavour here and I like the idea of the Foundation eventually figuring out that it's not simulating stuff but it feels…like this is the setting of a story where you haven't managed to tease the core narrative arc out yet?

The idea of playing with the conflict between 'using this to figure out how to handle containment breaches better' and 'not using this to prevent it spreading and reduce the risk of a containment breach here' could be fun; or a discussion of the ethics of causing harm in another universe instead could be good; but without something like this where it ends up y'know, escalating and coming to some kinda conclusion, I'm not sure it'd work.

item.title: SCP-XXXX A blessed exchange (Seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Mystery

Page Layout: Object description and containment are minimal, and main focus will be on testing logs. There will be 10-15 of them, starting with mundane, and increasing in strangeness.

Elevator Pitch: The object swaps two aspects (body parts/memories/reality of their life) of a person with a new one, seemingly from its "collection" of obtained aspects. Since an unknown number of exchanges have occurred, over an unknown time/places, it has an unknowable number of aspects in its collection.

Central Narrative: Minimal. The testing logs will add mystery around the objects age/origins and purpose, suggesting alien/extra-dimensional life. Since the object can alter reality, detailed records and logs need to be kept in order to keep track of reality alterations.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The object removes aspects of a person and gives a brand new one. The removal of aspects could kill or dramatically change a person, even removing people/companies/ideas related to them. The new aspects can be memories, new organs, or reality altering itself as well. The testing logs will start with mundane things, eg gaining memories of another person, growing a new limb etc, and will progress to stranger exchanges where friends/family cease to exist, or they gain non-human knowledge. Adding to the intrigue is that every aspect "given" is assumed to have been taken at some stage, suggesting that the object has altered reality many times in the past in unknown ways.

item.title: Re: (Seeking greenlight) Literally just straight fucking ice zombies
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

that converts people into "ice zombies" using unknown means.

What do you mean by 'ice zombie'? Like, beings made of ice that behave like zombies? Zombies who can control ice?

After a bit a "portal" (not really sure what it's going to be) to that universe opens up, and the foundation sends a research team into it.

My concern with this sentence is two fold: it's a passive unfolding of events, and I don't know what happens when the research team enters or why we care.

When I say 'it's a passive unfolding of events', what I mean is that there's nothing the Foundation are doing to try and achieve this, it's just, something which happens; which in turn means there's no 'will they succeed?' tension but there's also no narrative hook here because until this happens, there's no way to hint that this will happen.

On the flip side: there's no real indication of there being any consequences to this happening. It's like the culmination of the story, where we finally find out what is happening and the curtain is whipped back to reveal…nothing?

Fundamentally, my concern with this pitch is that it starts out sounding like a kinda generic zombie story with a slight twist of ice being involved, and then, instead of playing with that further, some stuff happens and a whole other universe is dragged in. It kinda feels like this is adding more complexity to the idea and introducing new elements in an attempt to be interesting, whereas if you actually wanted to make this work, you'd figure out how to do something interesting with the elements you already have.

IMO: this needs a shift in focus. Either the focus is this weird spot where anomalous things appear, and the Foundation trying to figure out why and how to stop it before they accidentally create a portal to the other universe and we learn something important about why this happens; or the focus should be on the ice zombies and the Foundation trying to deal with them, and the whole 'other universe' angle should be dropped. I think either thing could work, but I think blending them together like this is going to be unsatisfying cos you're forced to have the start of your article be effectively a bait and switch.

If you do this though, you're really going to have to consider the growth of the story: what changes in our understanding between the start and the end; how do the characters involved change; how do our feelings about this change; how do you get from a to b to c in a way that keeps a reader on board and excited for the journey.

item.title: Re: The Inventor
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

so he started to travel across world and he ended up in one of the sites of SCP Fundation.

How did he like…just end up in one of the sites of the Foundation? Was this a deliberate effort on his part or did it just kinda happen?

My core concern with this proposal is that the central narrative section falls into two pitfalls: it's extremely focussed on what the SCP does to the point where it doesn't even mention the Foundation; and it's also extremely flat.

The problem with the first is that a SCP article is written by the Foundation, which means that they're the POV character(s) for the story: it'll inevitably have to be told via the tests the foundation does, or the interviews they carry out, or the incident reports that they write, or via journal notes that they find; and so focussing so much on what the SCP is and what they do can be a mistake because it means the Foundation are just kinda…there?

The issue with the second is that there's no change throughout the story: it's expanding more on the context of The Inventor but a lot of this arc has happened already. Like, the inventor is ~4 billion years old, he's clearly come to terms with him having never run out of creativity, and so there's not really any growth? The Foundation doesn't learn to contain him better; there's no like, struggle from the inventor's aim being impossible; and so I'm left wanting more out of this.

I think this really could work and be an interesting story: I just think it needs you to figure out what the actual story within the article is. I feel like the most interesting angle is either the inventor coming to terms with his literal created purpose being impossible for him to complete; or for the foundation to attempt to utilise his inventiveness and then something happening as a result of this. At it's core, my issue is that this needs something interesting to happen with the pieces you've set up.

item.title: (Awaiting greenlights) The elite soldier.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Action.

Elevator Pitch: The elite operative is a soldier that is trapped inside a suit. The suit has many abilities. It can withstand heavy kinetic damage, it has bullet resistance against small ammunition for example a 9.mm bullet and it gives the soldier super human strength. But there are other abilities that are in-humane and cruel, gas containers attached to the suit, set of torture tools inside the suit, and explosives full with diffrent types of poisons.

Central Narrative: The story starts in a Anderson robotics factory. Anderson robotics made a deal with the U.S. army to create suits that would give soldiers anomalous abilities. The first suit was tested, the U.S. army closed the deal off after they saw what horrible things the suit can do such as: containers full with gas, a set of torture tools inside the suit, Diffrent types of poisons inside deadly explosives. Only 3 were made two are still missing and the third one a soldier still wears. The foundation is still looking for the two missing suits. The SCP foundation heard about the suits and found a suit with the soldier inside. Verbal communication was not affective since any sound that the soldier would make is drowned by the heavy metal suit. All attempts to get the soldier out of the suit are in-affective. After finding out the soldier could not be freed, he was interviewed via radio and agreed to use the suit he is trapped in to help the foundation. He was classed a Thaumiel SCP and assigned to MTF Alpha-9 ("Last Hope") And used in the field. He was shipped to Site-06-3 awaiting deployment.

The suit's abilities are explained with addendums and mission logs. And the only way to communicate with the soldier is via radio.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Although many "robotic suit" ideas and SCP's are on the site. My idea is unique because of two reasons. 1, the SCP's abilities. It's super-human strength, resistance to small bullets and kinetic energy. I have yet to see a robotic SCP with such abilities on the site. And 2, It's friendly-ness towards humans and it's will to help them with raids, containment and more that they ask for. I did not see any other robotic SCP do this.

Additional Notes: Since I am quite new if anyone would like to give tips about the Hook/Attention grabber it would be very helpful. Thanks!

item.title: Re: Quasi-Rewrites

I'm not a woman and I am fairly offended at this… so I would worry about anyone who identifies as female and how they might feel. Echoing all of the concerns mentioned above… I would also like to point out that the horrible misogyny angle of common horror tropes is not only offensive, it's boring.

Try to aim for something not meant to shock… because often times when we try to shock, we aim too low and end up writing offensive things… or more often, just boring things.

Think about something that makes you uneasy, and write an article about that, in a grounded contemplative way.

I would hope you are going to go back to the drawing board, but I just wanted to urge you to think about how others might respond to your proposal for the next idea.

item.title: A Thousand Door (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror, Exploration, Ambiance

Page Layout: Standard SCP Article with Explorations Logs towards the "doors"

Elevator Pitch: it revolves around a building called Lawang Sewu, a colonial-era building that has a thousand doors because it really does have lots of doors in it. Every door has its own theme about Colonialism History, the upper place or the ground floor is accessible by a tourist, but the underground section of the floor is forbidden by the public, and the whole building itself should be monitored and staffed with Foundation Guards.

Central Narrative: The narrative will focus on the exploration logs about these "doors" that are in the underground, at first it will be a normal abandoned underground room with an 1800-1900s theme, as the exploration goes deeper, it will get an even weirder and darker theme of the place itself, some of it may cause cognitive disturbances, and some may have an entity that is hostile and non-hostile. The Exploration team must explore the room to progress further into another room, the room itself appears to be not in order which results in every room they encounter is randomized every time they started the exploration.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Every room has its own theme, it tells how dark and cruel the colonization was. Tourists on the upper floor may see that colonization improved the country by a lot but in the underground, it tells the horrifying experience of being dictated by the upper echelon of that time. Tortured, discriminated, killed, etc by the colony. The Room expresses how the people back then were mistreated, some of the entities in the room being hostile because of it. The Foundation is still exploring the underground to know what really happened.

Additional Notes: I may add exploration logs also with some interviews with a non-hostile entity in the room to get a grasp of what does this room feels and its entity around it.

item.title: Re: The Bone Seer
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

The SCP is motivated by a zealous belief that a K-class scenario is coming soon, though it doesn't know when or how, and the details it describes do not match any known K-class scenarios.

I really like this idea of reading the bones but I am unconvinced about the entire thing centered around a vague K-class event. That's no way to build stakes.

I think this could work without the vague threat, make it something a bit more grounded… like the Seer is worried about being hunted by something or someone (but don't be vague, be mysterious), while you sell it with how upset/scared they are and are looking for security in containment. (this is just an idea, you don't have to take the suggestion of course)

This belief does however leave it completely cold and apathetic to individual lives, including its own, as well as highly cooperative with the Foundation, believing it will be necessary to try and piece the world together after the cataclysm.

also not convinced that being sure the world would end would then lead to these results… like maybe the cooperation, but why would it make the SCP apathetic about the individual lives? That's fine if you wanna make them cold towards individual lives, but it doesn't make much sense this would be the reason personally.

can then turn to the experiment logs to see how various test subjects deal with having the memories of others

Also not really sold on this idea, I don't think experiment logs is the way to go here. Instead you could summarize what research was done with the results and then unpack them in conversations or observation reports from the researchers.

Overall, I like the idea of the core anomaly… but I think some unpacking of the actual anomaly would be more interesting than the focus on some vague end of the world. Most of the compelling SCPs I have read have not had such HUGE stakes. I think this would work better with a more grounded relatable story about a person who can see into weird shit and how its affected them… Maybe some of the history of the practice, where this person has been/where they've used it before, and some unpacking of their psychological status as a result.

item.title: SCP-XXXX (Veracity)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Technical SCP including developments associated with the testing of this SCP. Focus on addendums and Incident Reports to describe the Foundation’s efforts to contain and understand this object.

+ Elevator Pitch:
– hide block

Elevator Pitch:
Foundation Discovery of GRU-P Experiments at New Research Area Kantubek located on the Vozdrozhdeniya Isthmus (Formerly island) in the now diminishing Aral Sea region near the Kazakhstan/Uzbekistan border. SCP-XXXX is a Polygraph machine with cognitohazardous properties which affect those exposed to the results produced by the machine making them believe with certainty and without question the accuracy and truth of statements analyzed by the machine, even when presented with factual evidence to the contrary (cognitive dissonance). Further experimentation reveals additional congnitohazards associated with the machine as well as evidence of suspected retrocausal effects generated by the machine. Much of the story development in the article will occur via incident reports filed by Foundation personnel.

+ Central Narrative:
– hide block

Central Narrative:
SCP-XXXX is one of many SCPs the Foundation currently contains (or is attempting to contain) at Research Area Kantubek, formerly a GRU-P research and development facility. Central tension focuses around GRU-P mismanagement of anomalous items and persons and the implications of containment breaches. I would like to expand the story of SCP’s at Research Area Kantubek as well as create a number of tales which describe the lives and personal experiences of Foundation Personnel working within this former GRU-P compound. While this article is just to begin seeding plot ideas and characters regarding this small-ish setting, I would like to develop it into a larger series spanning around 20-25 years of Foundation efforts occurring at this area as well as their interactions with other GOI’s (and the associated physical, emotional and political challenges Foundation Personnel face here).

+ Hook/Attention-Grabber:
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Focus on a relatively mundane object which is discovered to have exceptional properties beyond original Foundation expectations and the Foundations scramble to expand Special Containment Procedures.

+ Additional Notes:
– hide block

Additional Notes:
I’d like this article to be both enjoyable as a stand-alone read as well as effectively seed interest in the wider story regarding SCPs and Foundation Personnel at RA-Kantubek. I don’t want the first piece to be of too grand a scale as to overshadow future pieces, but it also needs to be involved enough as to hint at other developments and stories in RA-Kantubek. I’m also concerned about writing something too “big”, but I’m not sure how much content should be in a single SCP article to retain interest but also to decently seed plot points for future articles. Any input and feedback is welcome and appreciated!


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn
EDIT: Formatting updates per comments from Zyn. ~Archivist 346

item.title: Re: The Black Hourglass
item.content:encoded:
+Overall Thoughts
– hide block

Overall, I thought it was alright. You were worried about your dialogue, but it seemed fine to me (however, I'm not the best with dialogue, so you should definitely get a second opinion).

My first main concern is that you didn't cite your image. First, check the image use guidelines and make sure that your image is CC compliant. If it is, put a license box at the bottom of the page. If it isn't, you can't use it in your article. If you want to know where to find CC compliant images, I would recommend Wikimedia Commons and CCSearch.

My second issue are the test logs. The focus of your is on Licht's character arc, but your logs are pretty detached from that. You can also cut down on the description of SCP-####-A through -I by having there only be one button that lets Licht move outside of the flow of time, and then just letting him walk around outside of time instead of using multiple other buttons to do so.

+line-by-line
– hide block

SCP-#### has the ability to create a temporal anomaly capable of consuming the time of macroscopic life

"consuming time" is pretty vague. You explain the effect of this later in the paragraph, but I think you should find a better descriptor for the SCP's effect.

The activation time is inconsistent, along with the amount of time SCP-#### consumes.

I'd change this to "Both the activation time and the amount of time SCP-#### consumes1 are inconsistent."

SCP-#### appears to be designed to permanently attach itself to an humanoid individual. The requirements for this process to occur are as of yet unknown. It is also unknown if it is possible to remove SCP-#### without physically damaging the individual which it has attached to.

This makes it sound like SCP-#### is physically attached to an individual, when the recovery log shows that it just floats near them.

extreme gravitational lensing

I'd put a footnote briefly defining "gravitational lensing", since I imagine most readers won't know what that is (or maybe everyone knows what that is and it's just me).

it has been designated SCP-####-2

I'd change it to SCP-####-1 since you never mentioned -1.

with genetic matches to theirs were discovered at [DATA EXPUNGED]

I don't understand why this is redacted. I'd recommend reading this guide

I just happen to be in the wrong place

You don't need to change this since dialogue doesn't have to have perfect grammar, but "happen" should be "happened"

Subject entered within 10 meters of SCP-####. Immediately, SCP-#### began activating, and subject disappeared from the cell.

I'd change this to "SCP-#### activated immediately after subject entered within 10 meters of SCP-####." You can remove "subject disappeared from the cell" because the next couple sentences imply that the subject disappeared.

Subject 6 was found to have transported to a closed doorway, and suffered [DATA EXPUNGED]. Subject died █ minutes after initial recovery.

I'd change this to "Subject 6 was found to have been transported inside of a closed doorway and could not be recovered." Saying that they couldn't be recovered implies that they were located but died before they could be properly rescued.
